picks.title: OpenAI Auto Enabling Creative Enhancements In ChatGPT Ads
picks.rationale: From Oct 30, ChatGPT Ads will rewrite, translate, and resize advertisers' creative by default and can serve those versions without review. Every self-serve advertiser needs to check the opt-out setting before then.
picks.excerpt: OpenAI emailed ChatGPT Ads advertisers that from Oct 30 it will auto-enable 'creative enhancements' on new and existing self-serve campaigns, rewriting headlines and descriptions to fit the conversation, translating ad text, resizing images and optimizing destination URLs. The AI-adapted versions can run without advertiser review; opt-out is in Ads Manager.

picks.title: New Gemini tools for small business owners
picks.rationale: Google's own announcement connects Gemini to Google Ads, Shopify, and Canva and lets it take a brand kit to generate on-brand campaign visuals, which puts AI ad creative in front of small sellers.
picks.excerpt: Google launched a Gemini business landing page that connects to Google Ads, Business Profile, Workspace, Shopify and Canva, and can take a brand kit, fonts and palettes to generate on-brand visuals for product launches and marketing campaigns, with marketing and finance skills rolling out.

picks.title: AI Slop Sites Are On The Rise. Is Ad Tech Ready For Its New MFA Challenge?
picks.rationale: A DecryptAds study found more than 2,100 AI-generated made-for-advertising recipe sites carrying Fortune 500 ads. This is a new brand-safety problem in programmatic buying, and media buyers should audit their inclusion lists.
picks.excerpt: A DecryptAds study found more than 2,100 AI-generated recipe sites with fabricated author profiles, monetized through programmatic ads in the made-for-advertising playbook, carrying ads from blue-chip and Fortune 500 brands.

picks.title: Google Ads AI Max spotted automatically enabled in some Ad Grants accounts
picks.rationale: Google's AI Max for Search, which matches without keywords and writes its own ad text, is turning on by itself in nonprofit Ad Grants accounts. The broader AI matching can push CTR below the compliance threshold, so grant managers should check their campaign settings now.
picks.excerpt: Google Ads' AI Max for Search is showing up switched on in some nonprofit Google Ad Grants accounts without advertisers enabling it, expanding keywordless matching and auto-generating ad text from landing pages; since Ad Grants compliance hinges on CTR, broader AI matching could push accounts below the threshold. Google has not confirmed a grants-wide rollout.

picks.title: A startup offered free pizza if its AI agent ordered it. Chaos ensued.
picks.rationale: Hark spent $1M on a promo that paid for DoorDash pizza if its AI agent placed the order. That took the app to No. 1 in Apple's Lifestyle category, but the agent also failed orders, ran up unexpected charges, and asked for broad Gmail access. It is a concrete case of agentic checkout used to acquire customers, and of how that can backfire.
picks.excerpt: AI startup Hark ran a $1 million giveaway offering $30 DoorDash credit to users who downloaded Hark Pro and let its agent order a pizza; the promo pushed the app to No. 1 in Apple's Lifestyle category and Hark says it delivered nearly 20,000 pizzas, but many users hit failed orders, unexpected charges and broad Gmail-permission requests.
